scoring_notice: All scores are analyst judgments, not survey-derived probabilities, investment advice, or proof of willingness to pay. Evidence eligibility checks presence, not truth, independence, geography, freshness, or commercial validation.

opportunities.title: Human-reviewed AI client briefs for small professional-services firms
opportunities.buyer: Operations lead or managing partner at a 5–50-person bookkeeping or advisory firm
opportunities.problem: AI-assisted client drafts lack a lightweight review record tied to the exact approved version.

evidence.finding: July 2026 survey of 5,067 U.S. adults: AI users ranked accuracy 45%, trustworthiness 40%, and security/privacy 36% among choice factors. This consumer signal is not evidence of a bookkeeping firm's software budget.
2025 report says 58% of surveyed small businesses use generative AI, versus 40% in 2024. Adoption is not demand for this product.
GAO describes inaccurate outputs and data privacy/security risks in AI adoption. Government-focused risk corroboration, not SME market-size evidence.

SME AI adoption constraints include skills, data, finance and privacy/security. Reliable redaction and auditability remain engineering challenges; this MVP does not solve comprehensive data loss prevention.

opportunities.commercial_hypothesis: Offer a paid 30-day pilot for one client-brief workflow. Interview 10–15 firms; proceed only if at least two agree to paid pilots and can demonstrate recurring review pain.
opportunities.kill_criterion: Stop or change niche if interviews find no recurring problem, no budget owner, or existing bundled tools solve the workflow adequately.
opportunities.competition_risk: Platform governance suites and provider-native controls may bundle the feature. A review log alone is not a moat.
opportunities.geography_limit: Initial evidence is U.S. consumer/SMB and OECD, not validation of Indian demand.

opportunities.title: Invoice reconciliation and approved follow-up queue
opportunities.buyer: Owner/bookkeeper at a small B2B agency or consultancy
opportunities.problem: Overdue invoices and mismatched partial payments require manual review before sending accurate reminders.

evidence.finding: Intuit's January 2025 survey of 2,487 U.S. businesses with 0–100 employees: 56% were owed unpaid invoices, averaging $17,500; 47% had some invoices overdue over 30 days. Survey association, not causal impact or willingness to buy.

The unpaid-invoice problem motivates an engineering hypothesis: robust partial-payment, credit and dispute matching must precede reminder generation. The source does not benchmark reconciliation difficulty.

opportunities.competition_risk: Accounting vendors and AR tools already own integrations and provide reminders; generic reminder generation is poorly differentiated.
opportunities.commercial_hypothesis: Validate cross-system exceptions with five bookkeepers before building an accounting integration.

opportunities.title: Source-grounded local-business social draft approvals
opportunities.buyer: Owner or marketing lead of a local multi-location service business
opportunities.problem: Keeping fresh channel-specific content consistent consumes time and risks publishing stale offers or unsupported claims.

evidence.finding: Verizon/Morning Consult survey of 600 U.S. SMB decision-makers: 54% struggled to produce enough fresh content, while 73% wanted to expand to more channels. Perceptions are not demonstrated software purchasing intent.

36% of consumers reported lower interest in known AI-generated content versus 14% higher interest. Engineering hypothesis: grounded claims, freshness and review matter more than raw generation volume; not proof that this architecture changes outcomes.

opportunities.competition_risk: Crowded generator/scheduler market; fragile platform APIs and consent requirements. Draft/export only would avoid publishing risk but weaken differentiation.
opportunities.commercial_hypothesis: Test retention and qualified inquiries in a single vertical, not generated-post counts.
